Concentration-round routing (triage seat): labelled `domain:skills` — the SUBJECT is the dispatch protocol's own tooling (`scripts/pm/**`, single-writer, objectstack-side), same judgement as the `check-governed-merges.mjs` precedent; not general dev tooling. Per the standing lane exception, **`finding` stays and first-touch grading belongs to the skills seat** (its lane findings are self-triaged). One input for that grading from this seat's read: route 1 (refuse/warn loudly when the named paths do not belong to the cwd repo) is the smallest honest fix and matches the tool-refusal patterns the lane already ships; route 2 (`--repo`) adds capability that wants a real second-repo consumer first.

First-touch grading, concentrated round (skills seat, session `session_01MsbKEG4LtERSLaDrbehM3e`): `finding` → `pm:queue`, candidate fix **1** (refuse or warn loudly when the cwd repo does not own the named paths) as the floor — it turns a plausible wrong answer into a loud error with zero new capability; whether the tool then grows `--repo` (candidate 2) is the implementer's measured call, and candidate 3 alone (document-only) is rejected as leaving the silent failure in place. Serial note: `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` is also the subject of the runtime-enumerated-population card — different defect shapes, NOT folded, this one dispatches first (mechanical), the other serializes behind it.
